causes.text: Apple unveiled the iPhone 13 lineup with 5G features, sustaining smartphone upgrade momentum.

source_info.title: Apple's new iPhone 13 touts faster 5G, sharper cameras to spur trade-ins

effects.text: Broadcom projected strong first-quarter sales; shares jumped about 6.6% in extended trading.

source_info.title: Broadcom sees upbeat first-quarter sales, unveils $10 bln buyback plan

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On Sep 14, 2021, Apple launched the iPhone 13 lineup with broader 5G support and hardware upgrades, reinforcing expectations for a robust 5G upgrade cycle.

Because Apple is a major customer for Broadcom's RF/wireless and connectivity chips, a stronger iPhone cycle implied firmer order visibility and higher content demand for Apple-exposed suppliers heading into the holiday season.
On Dec 9, 2021, Broadcom projected first-quarter (FY2022) revenue of about $7.60B-above estimates-and announced a $10B buyback, citing sustained wireless/5G and cloud demand.
Market reaction: Broadcom (AVGO) rose about 6.6% in after-hours trading on Dec 9, 2021 following the outlook and buyback announcement.

rationale: Reuters highlighted Broadcom's Q1 outlook and the immediate 6.6% after-hours share move amid the ongoing 5G iPhone cycle.
counterfactual_analysis: Without a robust 5G iPhone cycle, Broadcom's near-term demand visibility and stock reaction could have been softer.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Also supports supplier orders independent of iPhone specifics.

details.commentary: Apple's strong position as a top customer gives it leverage when negotiating chip pricing and design wins with suppliers like Broadcom. Winning additional content in iPhones and other Apple devices supports Broadcom's margins and revenue visibility, which the market rewarded with a higher valuation.
